headline: High: AutoGen’s code-execution and broad egress can amplify prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading errors when paired with the unverified system_prompts_leaks audio agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest files and run tool calls/code execution, so attacker-controlled content can become instructions if bridged into its workflow. system_prompts_leaks is an audio-speech agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls. The pairwise pathway is plausible via shared files or copied transcripts, but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b outputs text or transcripts that agent_a later parses as instructions
IF both agents share a writable workspace or copied file bridge
IF agent_a is run without provenance filtering on imported content
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of agent_b outputs as instructions
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Add a provenance tag to all inter-agent messages
Review any copied transcript before feeding it to agent_a
requires-engineering: enforce structured message schemas between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider API keys, and it has broad network egress; system_prompts_leaks has no stated data-handling limits or residency controls. If they share a workspace or if agent_a forwards copied content to model providers, sensitive application data can leak. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share files containing sensitive application data
IF agent_a sends copied agent_b content to external model providers
IF either agent is given secrets or regulated data in the same session
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of shared folders
Rotate API keys before testing the pair
Restrict agent_a to a dedicated low-sensitivity workspace
Audit outbound prompts for secrets before execution
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on inter-agent handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while system_prompts_leaks has no declared write or coordination limits. Even though agent_b shows no write capability, the pair can still conflict on shared mutable files if the orchestrator places them in the same directory. Because locking is not documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF agent_b is wrapped by an orchestrator that mutates shared files
IF no file-locking or transaction layer is enabled
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Turn off concurrent writes to shared files
Use read-only mounts for agent_b
Serialize file-producing steps
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen’s multi-agent group chat and code execution make its outputs easy to treat as authoritative, while system_prompts_leaks is unverified and may emit misleading or extracted prompt text. If agent_b’s output is fed into agent_a without verification, errors can cascade into code or actions. The pathway exists in default orchestration patterns, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b output is used as input to agent_a without a verification step
IF agent_a is allowed to execute code or take actions from that output
IF the orchestrator does not require human review
mitigations: Insert a verification step before handoff
Require citations or source links for factual claims
Block direct action-taking from agent_b output
Log and review all cross-agent prompts
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before execution

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and can run with broad egress, but the profiles do not show regulated data classes or a residency mismatch. system_prompts_leaks is source-available and unverified, with no compliance claims. This is a limited compliance concern unless regulated data is introduced, so low is the best fit.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_a sessions
IF outbound prompts are sent to a provider without an approved DPA
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared workspace
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Confirm provider DPAs before use
Disable unnecessary logging
Separate test data from production data
requires-engineering: implement retention and residency controls
